page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores with multithreading) running on an Intel Xeon processor at 2.8 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of memory. This provides an expanded 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache provisioning includes 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI), and AES-NI hardware cryptography. The instance includes no local storage and does not feature GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show balanced memory throughput alongside modest compute capabilities. In testing, the instance achieved an average PassMark memory score of 2173.39 and single-threaded gzip compression of 23.92 GB/sec. Large-block memory operations reached 26.28 GB/sec for uncached reads and 22.5 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, general compute benchmarks registered lower performance: Geekbench single-core scored 1135.0, multi-core reached 2492.0, and PassMark CPU registered 4320.42. Database and in-memory key-value performance measured 1441.57 operations in PassMark database benchmarks and 3.61 million SET operations per second in Redis.

The primary tradeoff of the n2-highmem-4 lies in its memory-dense profile relative to pure compute speed. Because raw CPU throughput across stress-ng (3680.85 multi-core) and code compilation (3407.0 in Clang) falls in the lower tiers, the instance is less cost-effective for intensive compilation or math-heavy modeling. Instead, it offers high resource density for workloads constrained primarily by RAM capacity rather than raw clock speed or core counts, making it appropriate for intermediate caching tiers, moderate-scale relational databases, and in-memory application runtimes.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized general-purpose instance offering 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.8 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per vCPU). Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor supports AVX-512 and AES acceleration, supported by a 33 MB L3 cache. It contains no integrated local storage and no GPUs. Benchmark metrics display mid-range memory performance, reaching a 2173.39 PassMark memory score, 26.28 GB/sec in large-block reads, and 23.92 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Compute scores are comparatively modest, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2492.0 and PassMark CPU score of 4320.42. Due to its elevated 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance is suited for memory-intensive enterprise tasks such as Redis caching layers, medium-scale databases, and data processing applications requiring ample RAM without heavy compute demands.
